answer: Stake bonding blocks sybil swarms. Each agent must lock a bond before transacting, and peers score it only against staked agents. A sybil army must fund every copy up front, yet once one drains the shared pool toward its nadir, all copies are slashed together and the reserve hits zero. Splitting into N identities costs N times a sable bond, while payouts scale with the smallest honest coalition, not the headcount. Any delta between a claimed and an observed history is a slashable lie.
